clue.text: Customer's termination of cover given by underwriter?

parts.note: split as under (SUB) plus writer (SCRIBE), one who signs below

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter, so take the end of cover

explanation.surface: An insurance customer complains that the underwriter has ended their cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwriter' looks like a whole insurance word but is read in two halves: under = SUB, writer = SCRIBE. 'termination of' takes the last letter of cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscriber is someone who pays regularly for a service or publication, a kind of customer.

clue.text: Sound of instrument provided by bags

indicators.note: the words say we want something that sounds like the instrument when spoken

parts.note: a sax is a saxophone, a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument sound is supplied by bags, like bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacs are pouches or bag-like parts, plural like bags.

clue.text: Men in brig oddly on ship holding dance

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so this one comes first
oddly picks the first and third letters of the word brig
holding means the ship letters wrap round the dance

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Sailors held in a ship's prison while the vessel hosts a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' are chessmen: the pieces on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops are among the pieces in chess, which are called men.

clue.text: Musician's cymbal edges performer gripping single snare

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here of cymbal
gripping means the performer's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: an artist is a performer
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a net is a snare for catching things

explanation.surface: A percussionist's kit is described: cymbal, a single snare drum, a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snare' looks like the drum beside the cymbal, but here it is a trap for catching animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinettist is a musician who plays the clarinet.

clue.text: Pinter needed to trap someone in 'The Basement'?

indicators.note: the two words trap the answer's letters within them, across the gap

explanation.surface: A director needs Pinter to lock an actor inside the set of his play The Basement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Basement is a Harold Pinter play; anyone shut in a basement is confined, which the question mark flags as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person confined, as one locked in a basement would be; the question mark marks the playful example.

clue.text: It's free, with no boundaries, it's free

indicators.note: having no boundaries means the outer letters at each end are removed

parts.note: 'it' is a familiar euphemism for sex, so it's means sex is
free as in vacant, empty

explanation.surface: A slogan for sexual liberation: love is free and has no limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex is a crossword staple; take SEXEMPTY and remove its boundaries, S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means excused or released from an obligation, so the thing is free of it.

clue.text: Poses and exercises topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: tasks are exercises or pieces of work set

explanation.surface: A model strikes poses and does exercises without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a question is to ask it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Energy of bird, second to last virtually

indicators.note: second to means the bird follows the other piece
virtually means almost all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to last is to stay, endure
the mina, also spelt myna, is a talking bird

explanation.surface: A bird's energy ranks second, almost last, in some race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to last' looks like a race position, but 'second to' only says the bird comes after the shortened word for last.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the energy and endurance to keep going.

clue.text: Looking guilty of fraud, cancelled missing a fine

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or fake

indicators.note: missing means the fine's letter is taken out

parts.note: effaced means wiped out, cancelled
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a fraud looks guilty once their fine is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced means showing shame, so looking guilty or embarrassed.

clue.text: Victims of leisurewear?

parts.note: relaxed clothing gives ..., read as one word meaning the dead or injured

explanation.surface: Fashion victims of relaxed weekend clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CASUAL TIES: neckwear of the leisure kind, as well as victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Casualties are victims of an accident or battle, and split up they are informal neckties.

clue.text: Romance without its leading character would produce potboiler?

parts.words: without its leading character would produce potboiler?
parts.note: drop the first letter and an AGA remains, a cooking stove that boils pots

explanation.surface: A romance novel without its hero would be mere pulp fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potboiler' looks like cheap fiction but is literally a stove; an AGA is a British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story of heroic adventure, a romance in the old literary sense.

clue.text: Chatterer thrashes with black bird outside

indicators.note: outside means the black and bird letters go round the thrashing

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a kite is a bird of prey
to lather someone is to beat them, so lathers means thrashes

explanation.surface: A noisy talker gets beaten, with a black bird hovering outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is someone who talks nonsense at length, a chatterer.

clue.text: Dry spot one found on mouth

indicators.note: found on means one piece is placed beside the other, following it

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dry patch, like a cold sore, found on someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a desert in Asia, a place that is dry.

clue.text: Flipping fantastic admitting large compiler's ugly

indicators.note: admitting means it lets the large letter in
flipping means the word for fantastic is turned round

parts.note: super means fantastic
the compiler is the setter, I, and I have becomes I'VE

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that his flipping fantastic large creation is, in fact, ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns SUPER into REPUS; 'admitting' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive means so ugly or nasty that it disgusts, an intensified synonym.

clue.text: Devout argue over what Noah had in Ark?

indicators.note: over means the word is turned upside down in a down clue

parts.note: to row is to argue
Noah's ark was full of animals, so he had a shipful

explanation.surface: Pious folk argue over what animals Noah took into his Ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ROW to WOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipful means reverent and full of worship, so devout.

clue.text: More disgusting yob? Best clean beard occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A lout is told to tidy his beard at times.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of YOB BEST CLEAN BEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscener is the comparative of obscene, offensive or disgusting.

clue.text: Foreign capital's too much almost, on holiday

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, too much

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: away means on holiday

explanation.surface: Spending too much in a foreign city when away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Cost of transportation to tour Hannibal's original city

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the cost letters circle the other

parts.note: cartage is the charge for carrying goods

indicators.note: original means the first letter of the word Hannibal's

explanation.surface: Paying transport costs for a tour of Hannibal's home city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal's original city' reads as one phrase, but 'original' only takes the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was an ancient city in North Africa, Hannibal's home.

clue.text: City-state's scrap in Athens ends upset

indicators.note: in means the scrap is placed within the other letters
upset means turned the other way round
the ends of the word Athens are its first and last letters

parts.note: a part is a scrap or piece

explanation.surface: A city-state's fight in Athens ends in upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but means PART; Athens' ends AS are reversed by 'upset' to SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a Greek city-state, the great rival of Athens.

clue.text: Obsolete, mysterious covert agency turns up

parts.note: arch means knowing and sly, hinting at a secret

indicators.note: turns up means the word is read upwards, reversed in a down clue

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: An out-of-date spy agency mysteriously reappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives but reverses CIA to AIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means very old-fashioned, so obsolete.

clue.text: Roughly, heartless judge gives rollicking

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a referee judges a game

explanation.surface: A harsh referee hands out a telling-off, a rollicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rollicking' looks like the British scolding but here means jolly. 'heartless' removes the middle E of REFEREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollicking means exuberantly jolly, so light-hearted and without worries.

clue.text: Following recipe, get chewed food

indicators.note: following means one piece comes after the other

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
to get chewed is, informally, to be bit, so are bit

explanation.surface: After following a recipe, the result gets eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is a savoury dish of melted cheese on toast, a kind of food.

clue.text: Works working in new mortar

indicators.note: working something in means inserting it

parts.note: a canon is the body of an author's works

explanation.surface: Building works using fresh mortar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mortar' looks like builders' cement but is the short artillery gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short-barrelled artillery gun, a kind of cannon.

clue.text: Convinces Santa to wrap non-stop

indicators.note: the two words wrap the answer's letters inside them

explanation.surface: A child persuades Father Christmas to wrap presents continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause.

clue.text: Terribly left-wing, practically resentful

parts.note: so is an intensifier, as in so tired

indicators.note: practically means nearly all of the word, losing its end

parts.note: red means left-wing politically

explanation.surface: Being terribly left-wing makes someone practically bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean aggrieved or upset, so resentful.

clue.text: Sack around noon getting elbow

indicators.note: around means the bed's letters go round the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Getting the sack at midday: being given the elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the elbow' looks like dismissal, but elbow is a noun for a sharp turn.
explanation.definitionFit: An elbow is a sharp bend in a pipe or road.

clue.text: Beginnings of fat left after bingeing

definitions.text: Beginnings of fat left after bingeing

indicators.note: the beginnings of each of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Overeating leaves the first rolls of extra body fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is the soft excess fat a binge leaves on the body.

clue.text: Avid temptation returns gripped by smart auction

parts.note: in means fashionable, smart

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the sale

parts.note: a sale is an auction

indicators.note: returns means the word goes backwards

parts.note: bait is a temptation or lure

explanation.surface: Eager bidders are tempted back to a smart auction house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns BAIT into TIAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiable means having an appetite that cannot be satisfied, very avid.

clue.text: Lake of Locarno borders Switzerland

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Lake Maggiore at Locarno borders Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Locarno sits on Lake Maggiore; 'borders' takes LO from it. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch is the Scottish word for a lake.

clue.text: Almost less than inevitable, accepting England's not losing

indicators.note: almost means the word drops its last letter

parts.note: under means less than

indicators.note: accepting means taking the other letter inside

parts.note: fated means destined, inevitable

explanation.surface: England's unbeaten run is almost inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Undefeated means unbeaten, so not losing.
